sections.title: Building the review panel for testing
sections.what: Bundles the review panel component and its React helpers into one script, so the test can run it without starting the app.
sections.why: Lets a Node test check the real component output.
sections.watch_out: The frontend folder path must match the real layout or the build fails.

sections.name: module
sections.title: Rendering and checking each review
sections.what: Runs the bundle in a sandbox, renders every committed review, checks required phrases and no NaN, and tests empty input and a malicious link.
sections.why: Checks what the user would see rather than the internal code.
sections.watch_out: The malicious-link check only covers the first field, so other fields are not tested for unsafe links.

summary: Checks that the evidence review panel renders correctly for each committed project review and that unsafe reference links are removed.
purpose: Makes sure the review panel shows the right text and does not show broken numbers or dangerous links.
why: Likely reason: reviewers rely on this panel to judge withheld values, so it must not show broken or unsafe content.
how: Bundles the React component into one script with esbuild, runs that script in an isolated sandbox, renders each committed review, and checks for required phrases and the absence of NaN. Then tests empty input and a reference with a javascript link and script tag.
inputs: The frontend component folder and the committed resolution JSON file.
outputs: A PASS line, or a failed assertion.
risks: Checks exact wording, so any change to the panel text fails the test. The malicious-link check only changes the first field.
debug: If bundling fails, check the component import path and that react and react-dom are installed. If a phrase check fails, compare the expected text with the component.
